recs.stt: The Case for a Teacher Bar Exam
recs.x:
had these MOOC's been available. However, I did have enough personal curiosity to pursue these things. In college now, I'm not "spoon fed" anymore, it is my responsibility to do well, and seek out help if I am struggling. I am just curious where people think that line is drawn, and if it's different for everyone or not. I am for the Bar exam - for goodness's sake, we still have teachers trying to teach Creationism!

One of my favorite videos on reforming education, from a very logical perspective from Sir Ken Robinson. Bonus: it's pictorially animated!
 [link]

The true solution is to revamp our country's education system and provide a framework that can accommodate the wide variety of personalities that come into the classroom. Instead of forcing children to think one way, we should let them think the way they NATURALLY think, and flourish with their native mindset.

I strongly recommend this eye-opening video for those of you who haven't already seen it: [link]

recs.stt: A non-moral dilemma about cheating, but it brings up some points (2019)
recs.x:
Trying to put kids in a system that is boxed due to constraints of age, time, subjects and grades is very harmful for the real development of individual kids. Kids understand this and get disengaged from the system but still have to force themselves to follow along because they are not provided with an alternative.

^ [link]

recs.stt: Academic acceleration in gifted youth: a 35-year longitudinal study
recs.x:
I feel like my entire time in school was spent getting it out of the way so I could study things that genuinely interested me. I would love for my children to not feel that same constraint, but instead feel free to go deeper at their own pace.

I'd recommend this talk by Sir Ken Robinson on this topic generally: [link]
